# Board nomination.
Nominate yourself or another owner for your association's board of directors. We pass every nomination to the board and include it in the election process your bylaws set.

## Submit a nomination.
Include the nominee's name and unit, and a short statement about why they want to serve.

- **[773.728.0652](tel:+17737280652)** Monday to Friday, 9:00 AM to 5:00 PM

- **[service@centerpointmgmt.com](mailto:service@centerpointmgmt.com)** Replies within one business day

- **5107 N Western Ave, Suite 1S** Chicago, IL 60625

## How nominations work.
Your association's bylaws and the election notice set who may serve, how many seats are open, and the deadline for nominations. Send your nomination before that deadline. Owners in good standing are generally eligible, but the specific rules for your community control, and management will tell you if a nomination cannot be accepted.

If you are nominating someone else, confirm with them first that they are willing to serve. A short candidate statement helps owners decide; if your association distributes statements with the ballot or meeting notice, we use the text you send.

Learn more about [Illinois board elections, proxies, and ballots](https://www.centerpointmgmt.com/blog/illinois-condo-board-elections-proxies-ballots) and how to prepare for the [annual meeting](https://www.centerpointmgmt.com/blog/illinois-association-annual-meeting-guide).

## Common questions.

### When is the nomination deadline?
It is set by your bylaws and stated in the election notice. If you do not have the notice, call or email our office and we will tell you.

### Do I need to be an owner to serve?
In most associations directors must be unit owners, and some bylaws add requirements such as being current on assessments. Your governing documents decide.

### Will my nomination appear on the ballot?
Eligible nominations received before the deadline are included in the election process your bylaws describe. Some associations also accept nominations from the floor at the meeting.
